title: Indus Operational System: A Formal Model of Harappan Administrative Notation
description: Complete formal reconstruction of the Indus script as a finite-state operational system for institutional validation. This work presents a novel interpretation of the Indus script not as a phonetic language, but as a mathematical protocol for administrative record-keeping, implemented as a finite automaton with 6 states and 417 catalogued symbols.
references: Parpola, A. (1994). Deciphering the Indus Script. Cambridge University Press.
Mahadevan, I. (1977). The Indus Script: Texts, Concordance and Tables. Archaeological Survey of India.
Wells, B. (2011). Epigraphic Approaches to Indus Writing. Oxbow Books.
Farmer, S., Sproat, R., & Witzel, M. (2004). The Collapse of the Indus-Script Thesis. Electronic Journal of Vedic Studies, 11(2).
Rao, R. P. N., et al. (2009). Entropic Evidence for Linguistic Structure in the Indus Script. Science, 324(5931).
